Their findings, [published in *Nature Machine Intelligence*](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-026-01268-y), suggest that adding more AI agents to a system is not always beneficial, as a single capable agent can perform better on some tasks than multi-agent systems. "The project started from a simple question: What actually makes a good AI agent?" Yubin Kim, first author of the paper, told Tech Xplore. "We see single-agent and multi-agent systems being used widely, while the choice of agent system design is often made manually, based on intuition or convention. It was not clear to us whether adding more agents always makes a system better. "So, we wanted to step back and ask more fundamental questions, like when does collaboration help? When can it hurt? What properties of the model, task or coordination structure determine the outcome? highlights.content: [![WisdomTree](/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fwisdomtree-logo-navy-2024.png&w=384&q=75&dpl=dpl_2SDRZt2PBXcZ57Z3Sbyr3K1KVZd5)](/us) ![](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Ff8796olh%2Fglobal-prod%2F09dae818365526f182f99173d699960ef786f3af-1920x1920.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C674%2C1920%2C573%26w%3D1340%26h%3D400%26fit%3Dcrop%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) [Back to Blog](/us/insights/blog) ## What NVIDIA's August 2026 Print Actually Tells Us About the AI Buildout Published September 2, 2026 [![Christopher Gannatti, CFA](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Ff8796olh%2Fglobal-prod%2F6035febbdd70b8151ded349c5c51f5ede83a9c61-1024x1024.png%3Fw%3D128%26h%3D128%26fit%3Dcrop%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75)](/us/insights/contributors/christopher-gannatti) [Christopher Gannatti, CFA](/us/insights/contributors/christopher-gannatti) Global Head of Research ### Key Takeaways * NVIDIA’s August 2026 results suggest the AI infrastructure bottleneck is shifting from GPUs toward memory, power and advanced packaging, reinforcing the opportunity across [WisdomTree Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Fund’s (WTAI)](/us/products/megatrends/wtai) diversified semiconductor and infrastructure holdings. * AI investment is broadening beyond traditional hyperscalers as neoclouds, private capital and NVIDIA-backed financing help fund the next phase of capacity growth, potentially expanding the demand base for AI infrastructure. * Rising revenue per gigawatt and sustained hyperscaler spending support the infrastructure-led AI thesis, while [WTAI](/us/products/megatrends/wtai) offers broader exposure to the physical buildout and the [WisdomTree U.S. Quality Growth Fund (QGRW)](/us/products/equity/qgrw) concentrates more heavily on NVIDIA and the mega-cap platforms financing it. NVIDIA's fiscal second-quarter results generated the predictable wave of headlines. For example: * A beat-and-raise quarter * A $300 price target chorus among sell-side analysts * A stock that shrugged off a soft gross-margin outlook to hold its gains However, the more useful exercise, we think, is to treat the print less as a single company's earnings event and more as a high-resolution readout on the state of the AI infrastructure buildout, such that we can learn something about where the bottlenecks are moving, who is funding the next leg of spending, and whether the "infrastructure" layer of the AI stack still commands as much of the value chain as it did a year ago. Put bluntly, margin percentage compresses, but gross profit dollars still rise. The more telling number, in our view, is what NVIDIA did about it. *Total supply and capacity commitments more than doubled quarter over quarter, from roughly $119 billion to $279 billion, overwhelmingly tied to memory procurement.*2 NVIDIA is now locking up multi-year high bandwidth memory (HBM) and dynamic random access memory (DRAM) supply with the same urgency it once reserved for advanced packaging and wafer capacity at its foundry partners. It’s interesting to see the physical constraint on how fast the AI buildout can scale shifting one layer down the stack, from logic to memory. #### **2. It will show up switched on inside a tool your institution already runs, added in an update to software that was up for renewal anyway. That’s how AI agents are spreading across higher education, through systems already in place, and faster than most institutions can write rules for them. Most Chief Information Officers (CIOs) know the term by now. Far fewer have a clear picture of what agents do, how they differ from their chatbot predecessors, and what it’ll actually take to govern them. That's worth sorting out before the agents outnumber the policies. ## What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot? An AI agent is software that acts autonomously on your behalf, within the constraints you set. It completes tasks, makes decisions, and coordinates across systems to reach a shared outcome. A chatbot *responds*, while an agent *acts*. That one-word difference carries most of the governance weight. This autonomy is exactly what raises the stakes. Agents reach into more systems, touch more data, and produce outcomes that are harder to audit than any single chatbot reply. Knowing what your agents are doing, and whether they’re doing it consistently, becomes a governance question as much as a technical one. ### **Real-world examples of institutional AI agents:** * At MIT’s Sloan School, Tutor AI walks students toward answers with hints rather than handing them over, so the work stays theirs.1 * At Michigan State’s Broad College, an advising agent wired directly into the registration system builds requirement-aware academic plans for each student.2 ## What happens when one agent becomes many? One agent is manageable. The trouble starts when a campus is running dozens: some stood up by IT, some adopted inside departments, and some switched on automatically in enterprise apps that were already up for renewal. This is the same AI adoption wave reshaping the rest of campus, only moving faster. By the end of 2026, 40% of enterprise applications will have task-specific AI agents built in, up from less than 5% in 2025.3 That shift is arriving in the tools institutions are renewing right now. Most of those agents are landing in exactly the categories institutions govern least. In the [research Superhuman conducted with Higher Ed Dive’s Studio](https://highereddive.tradepub.com/free/w_defa11253/?ref=blog.superhuman.com), 87%of institutions’ AI policies cover generative AI tools, but only 64% cover productivity agents and 59% cover academic support agents. “This is one of the most interesting tensions in higher ed right now,” says Yolanda Wiggins, senior researcher at Superhuman. “Institutions are still very much trying to catch up with just how quickly AI adoption is happening, especially informally, across campus.” Picture an orchestra before the conductor arrives. Every musician is capable and every instrument works, but without coordination you get noise instead of music. Orchestration is the conductor. Here’s What That Means.](https://storage.ghost.io/c/c7/8e/c78e4b36-4930-4765-917f-f40bc2da20ee/content/images/size/w900/2026/08/311989-grammarly-ss-made-by-institutions-blog-ai-agents-are-already-in-your-institution-Blog-Header-1520x800-1.png) [![Superhuman Team](https://storage.ghost.io/c/c7/8e/c78e4b36-4930-4765-917f-f40bc2da20ee/content/images/size/w320/2025/12/Hero_400x400-1.jpg)](https://blog.superhuman.com/author/superhuman/) Contributor: [Superhuman Team](https://blog.superhuman.com/author/superhuman/) Share on: The next AI agent on your campus probably won’t arrive through a purchase decision. It will show up switched on inside a tool your institution already runs, added in an update to software that was up for renewal anyway. That’s how AI agents are spreading across higher education, through systems already in place, and faster than most institutions can write rules for them. Most Chief Information Officers (CIOs) know the term by now. Far fewer have a clear picture of what agents do, how they differ from their chatbot predecessors, and what it’ll actually take to govern them. That's worth sorting out before the agents outnumber the policies. ## What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot? An AI agent is software that acts autonomously on your behalf, within the constraints you set. It completes tasks, makes decisions, and coordinates across systems to reach a shared outcome. A chatbot *responds*, while an agent *acts*. That one-word difference carries most of the governance weight. This autonomy is exactly what raises the stakes. Agents reach into more systems, touch more data, and produce outcomes that are harder to audit than any single chatbot reply. Knowing what your agents are doing, and whether they’re doing it consistently, becomes a governance question as much as a technical one. ### **Real-world examples of institutional AI agents:** * At MIT’s Sloan School, Tutor AI walks students toward answers with hints rather than handing them over, so the work stays theirs.1 * At Michigan State’s Broad College, an advising agent wired directly into the registration system builds requirement-aware academic plans for each student.2 ## What happens when one agent becomes many? One agent is manageable. The trouble starts when a campus is running dozens: some stood up by IT, some adopted inside departments, and some switched on automatically in enterprise apps that were already up for renewal. This is the same AI adoption wave reshaping the rest of campus, only moving faster. By the end of 2026, 40% of enterprise applications will have task-specific AI agents built in, up from less than 5% in 2025.3 That shift is arriving in the tools institutions are renewing right now. Most of those agents are landing in exactly the categories institutions govern least. In the [research Superhuman conducted with Higher Ed Dive’s Studio](https://highereddive.tradepub.com/free/w_defa11253/?ref=blog.superhuman.com), 87%of institutions’ AI policies cover generative AI tools, but only 64% cover productivity agents and 59% cover academic support agents. “This is one of the most interesting tensions in higher ed right now,” says Yolanda Wiggins, senior researcher at Superhuman. “Institutions are still very much trying to catch up with just how quickly AI adoption is happening, especially informally, across campus.” Picture an orchestra before the conductor arrives. Every musician is capable and every instrument works, but without coordination you get noise instead of music. Orchestration is the conductor. Unlike AI chatbots, agents function independently; they can plan, execute tools, and engage with real-time data.  The main challenge of this independence is that errors can compound through later steps and corrupt the output, leading to wasted tokens and failed system integration. To prevent this, AI agent evaluation is essential. This is a technical checklist that helps developers make sure these systems are ready for real-world use. The key objective is to track every decision an agent takes from the initial plan to the final execution. This article covers agent types, frameworks, and metrics. LLMs.titleZh: Insilico Medicine releases frontier AI models for drug discovery
LLMs.content: ![News-Medical](https://www.news-medical.net/themes/Standard/images/nm-logo-4.png) ![An AZoNetwork Site](https://www.news-medical.net/images/an-azonetwork-site.svg) ## Top Health Categories ## ×Top Health Categories # Insilico Medicine releases frontier AI models for drug discovery Insilico Medicine, a clinical-stage generative artificial intelligence (AI)-driven drug discovery company, today announced the release of a series of frontier specialist models for chemistry and biology, trained through its MMAI Gym for Science framework. Across chemistry and biology, the models demonstrate state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on more than 50 benchmark tasks. For years, language models have been seen as versatile conversational tools, but when it came to complex, data-scarce problems in drug discovery, specialized computational methods held the upper hand. With MMAI Gym, we are proving that language-model architectures, when trained with domain-specific multi-task precision, can move far beyond high-level general knowledge. They are now competing with and outperforming dedicated scientific methods on real-world chemistry and geroscience benchmarks, marking a fundamental shift toward truly predictive AI for human health." Alex Zhavoronkov, Ph.D., founder and CEO of Insilico Medicine Historically, low-data drug discovery tasks such as ADMET and target potency prediction have been dominated by specialized models developed specifically for molecular data. Language models have largely remained outside this competitive landscape. The latest results from MMAI Gym suggest that this is beginning to change, with language-model-based specialists now matching or outperforming established approaches on selected tasks. The models released through MMAI Gym are small language models trained into scientific specialists. Each model is fine-tuned for a defined category of scientific tasks and trained across multiple related problems within that category. These specialists are benchmarked directly against established computational methods using the same datasets and train-test splits. All baseline models were re-trained and run under the same evaluation setup and ground truth data splits, enabling head-to-head comparison rather than relying on scores reported on public leaderboards. The current set of chemistry models includes language-model-based specialists for chemical synthesis, ADMET prediction, and potency prediction across GPCR and kinase panels. For ADMET prediction, the specialist was evaluated across 28 tasks and achieved SOTA-level performance relative to established computational methods, with particularly strong results across drug-drug interaction risk, cytotoxicity, and pharmacokinetic properties. Accurate prediction of these properties can help identify liabilities earlier and support compound prioritization before more resource-intensive experimental studies. As a category-focused model, it can evaluate multiple ADMET-related endpoints using a single model rather than relying on separate models for each individual property. Furthermore, the model delivered the strongest overall performance on a held-out experimental set spanning 14 properties from the Drug Candidate Essentials benchmark, outperforming established SOTA baselines. For target activity prediction, two protein family-focused models were trained: one for GPCRs, covering 44 receptors, and one for kinases, covering 67 enzymes. In both categories, the models achieved SOTA-level IC50 prediction performance on selected targets. These models can support a range of drug discovery applications, from virtual screening and lead prioritization to the design of multi-target compounds and selectivity profiling to identify and minimize potential off-target activity. For chemical synthesis, the models are specialized for single-step retrosynthesis and are built on Liquid AI's compact 2.6B-parameter architecture. AI Product.content: # [Office of the CIO](/) ## [Technology Services](https://ts.vcu.edu) # AI Tools and Technologies VCU Technology Services licenses a variety of generative AI tools that are vetted, secured and available to VCU faculty, staff and students to use for free. See our list of enterprise tools below for more information, including approved data designations. **Microsoft Copilot** VCU has licensed Microsoft Copilot, a generative artificial intelligence chatbot for all faculty, staff, and students to use for free. Navigate to [go.vcu.edu/copilot](https://go.vcu.edu/copilot "Microsoft Copilot login") and login with your VCU email address and password. Copilot is built with the same security, privacy, and compliance standards as other Microsoft products. Our licensed access to Copilot is approved for Category 2 data and ensures that your prompts and Copilot’s responses are: * Not available to other customers * Not used to train or improve any third-party products or services (such as OpenAI models) * Not used to train or improve Microsoft AI models Please use our [Data Classification Tool](https://itgovernance.vcu.edu/security/data-classification/) to determine the sensitivity of your data and always minimize the data you provide GenAI tools.  **Important update**: as of November 2024 the Copilot app integration and file upload features no longer work for all VCU accounts. Microsoft now requires OneDrive to be enabled for this feature and we do not currently have OneDrive available for all VCU accounts. **Google Gemini** Google Gemini is a generative artificial intelligence chatbot for licensed all faculty, staff, and students to use for free. Navigate to [gemini.google.com](https://gemini.google.com/) and login with your VCU email address and password. Our licensed access to Gemini is approved for Category 2 data and ensures that your prompts and Gemini’s responses are: * Not available to other customers * Not used to train or improve any third-party products or services (such as OpenAI models) * Not used to train or improve Google AI models Please use our [Data Classification Tool](https://itgovernance.vcu.edu/security/data-classification/) to determine the sensitivity of your data and always minimize the data you provide GenAI tools. **Adobe Firefly** Adobe Firefly is a generative AI tool that enhances creativity by generating high-quality images, text effects, and other visual content based on user prompts. New Adobe Firefly features such as generative fill are now integrated directly within Adobe apps such as Photoshop and Illustrator allowing creators to quickly and easily change backgrounds, generate and move objects, and expand images seamlessly. AI Product.content: SecurityBrief US - Technology news for CISOs & cybersecurity decision-makers [![SecurityBrief US logo](/brands/sb-new-logo.svg) United States](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.com) ![Reco launches Browser Guard for enterprise AI security](https://securitybrief.news/uploads/story/2026/09/03/Ofer_Klein-story-318128.webp) [Data Protection](https://securitybrief.news/tag/data-protection) [Digital Transformation](https://securitybrief.news/tag/digital-transformation) [Cloud Security](https://securitybrief.news/tag/cloud-security) # Reco launches Browser Guard for enterprise AI security Wed, 2nd Sep 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://securitybrief.news/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) Reco has launched Browser Guard, a browser-based security product for enterprise AI use designed to address prompt injection, data leakage and unauthorised actions. The launch reflects a shift in how employees use artificial intelligence tools at work, with much of that activity now taking place in web browsers rather than in software already monitored by security teams. Browser Guard inspects prompts and agent activity in the browser, then matches that activity with information about the user, the data involved, the destination, the account type and the stated business purpose, according to Reco. The product is aimed at organisations trying to manage the spread of AI assistants, copilots, coding agents and automated workflows used by staff in day-to-day tasks. These interactions can create risks when security teams lack visibility into who is using a tool, what information is being entered and where the resulting actions are directed. **Browser focus** Reco is targeting a part of the market where AI use often begins outside approved channels. Browser Guard can identify AI tools, browser extensions and personal accounts used by employees beyond sanctioned systems, giving security teams visibility into whether business data is being shared. That focus on browser activity addresses what security specialists often describe as shadow AI, where workers adopt consumer or personal AI services without formal approval. In those cases, the concern is not only the tool itself but also where company data is sent and how far automated agents can act on a user's behalf. Agents create a broader set of risks than a single prompt because they can retrieve context, call tools and carry out actions, Reco said. Browser Guard is intended to assess the identity behind an agent's action, the data it can access and whether the behaviour aligns with company policy before allowing, guiding or blocking the activity. **Policy controls** The product adds a layer of context to each interaction by identifying the user, the data, the destination, the account type and the business purpose behind it. That information is intended to help security teams make policy decisions as the activity takes place rather than after the event. For companies adopting AI tools across business functions, the challenge has grown beyond maintaining lists of approved software. Security teams are increasingly being asked to judge the behaviour of AI systems embedded in browsers, messaging tools and coding environments, especially when those systems can trigger external actions or move data between services. "AI security is not just about knowing which tools employees use," said Ofer Klein, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Reco. They touch on different areas of development, but we will mainly talk about web development. If there's a project worth adding to the next collection, feel free to write about it in the comments, and maybe it will be included. --- ## 1. 🤖 [OpenWork](https://openworklabs.com) - The open source Claude Cowork alternative. And we will continue, of course, with AI projects. This tool will allow you to work in one convenient interface with many popular LLMs. OpenWork is the desktop app that lets you use 50+ LLMs. [💎 Check out the OpenWork repository ☆](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork) --- ## 2. 💻 [T3 Code](https://t3.codes) - The open-source control plane for coding agents. If you know a YouTuber like Theo, then you should know this project. It's an OpenCode alternative that lets you work with AI in an easy-to-use chat interface. It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app (iOS, Android), web app and Electron-based desktop app. [💎 Check out the T3 Code repository ☆](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code) --- ## 3. ⚙️ [Summarize](https://summarize.sh) - Point at any URL or file. Get the gist. The first project is a small tool for extracting short info of content. Summarize was created by one of the creators of the well-known OpenClaw. Fast summaries from URLs, files, and media. [💎 Check out the Summarize repository ☆](https://github.com/steipete/summarize) --- ## 4. 👾 [Godot](https://godotengine.org) - Free and open source 2D and 3D game engine A **truly legendary** engine like Unity or Unreal Engine for games. If you are a game developer, you should know this project. From pet projects for the university to multi-million dollar games - it gives it all. Infra & Chips.content: [Subscribe](https://newsroom.equinix.com/email-alerts) Press Release ## Equinix Accelerates AI Inference for Enterprises with NVIDIA and Together AI September 2, 2026 SHARE * [Share this page on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsroom.equinix.com%2Findex.php%3Fs%3D2429%26item%3D125345 "Linkedin Share") * [Share this page on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsroom.equinix.com%2Findex.php%3Fs%3D2429%26item%3D125345 "Facebook Share") * [Share this page on X](https://twitter.com/share?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsroom.equinix.com%2Findex.php%3Fs%3D2429%26item%3D125345 "Twitter Share") * ![](https://mmx.prnewswire.com/media/MS1980177/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live.jpg?id=OA2925142 "Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live") [View File](https://newsroom.equinix.com/2026-09-02-Equinix-Accelerates-AI-Inference-for-Enterprises-with-NVIDIA-and-Together-AI#assets_130:20196) [Download File](https://mmx.prnewswire.com/media/MS1980177/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live.jpg?id=OA2925142&p=original) Equinix® Inference Exchange - Bringing inference closer to where data, users and applications live *Equinix Inference Exchange combines NVIDIA Enterprise Reference Architectures, Together AI's inference platform and Equinix's global infrastructure to optimize deployment speed, flexibility and cost efficiency* REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Sept. 2, 2026 /[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/)/ -- [Equinix, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=1428223178&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.equinix.com%2F&a=Equinix%2C+Inc.) (Nasdaq: EQIX), the world's digital infrastructure company®, today announced a significant expansion of its longtime collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Equinix® Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI. As AI scales across models, providers and geographies, where inference runs is a strategic imperative that determines performance, cost and governance. Put bluntly, margin percentage compresses, but gross profit dollars still rise. It’s interesting to see the physical constraint on how fast the AI buildout can scale shifting one layer down the stack, from logic to memory. #### **2.
